page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmgn8t.32xlarge is an x86_64 bare-metal GPU-accelerated server instance designed for high-density compute and graphics workflows. It is powered by Intel Xeon 6462C processors clocked at 3.3 GHz, offering 128 dedicated vCPUs. The host is configured with 1024.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is provided by 8 NVIDIA Ada Lovelace architecture GPUs delivering a combined total of 192 GB of VRAM.

Network connectivity features a high baseline bandwidth of 170 Gbps, enabling fast data ingestion and node-to-node synchronization in distributed environments. A notable architectural tradeoff is the absence of bundled local storage, meaning all persistent data volumes and operating system disks must be provisioned via remote block or object storage over the network. Zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

From an efficiency perspective, the concentration of 8 dedicated GPUs alongside 1 TB of system RAM and 128 dedicated execution threads provides significant compute density within a single host. This architecture reduces multi-node networking overhead for workloads that fit within a 192 GB aggregate GPU VRAM footprint. Primary workload applications include parallel AI model inference, graphics virtualization, rendering pipelines, video transcode farms, and GPU-accelerated high-performance computing simulations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmgn8t.32xlarge is a dedicated bare-metal GPU instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 128 dedicated Intel Xeon 6462C vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz, coupled with 1024.0 GB of memory to yield an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. Hardware acceleration is driven by 8 NVIDIA Ada Lovelace GPUs providing 192 GB of total VRAM. Network operations are supported by a 170 Gbps baseline interface, though the instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations. With dense compute and memory capacity, this instance is suited for GPU-accelerated computing, AI inference, 3D rendering, video processing pipelines, and data-intensive analytical workloads requiring significant parallel throughput.
